review_reference: Owner decisions in chat by D-Eminence, 2026-11-05, relayed by the coordinator, for 0108 (records processing cover). D-a (lifetime), about 12:00 UTC: the owner answered "recommended" to removing the 24-hour bound: staff whose direct-care access to the patient is active may do records processing (purpose healthcare-operations, read_records or write_records) for as long as that access lasts, superseding the 24-hour bound of decision 34(1) (0104 D7). D-b (shares), about 12:00 UTC, an AskUserQuestion answer: "Yes, shares count (Recommended)" to the question "Should a patient SHARE also let that staff member bring in the patient's paper records (OCR)?", option text "Any active access the patient gave (approval, Access PIN or share) lets that staff member at that facility bring in paper records for as long as the access lasts. Under-18s, deny choices and the OCR permission still apply. The share screen will tell patients this." Any share level, view_only included, covers records-processing read and write (under healthcare-operations: creating a job and getting or listing jobs are read; retrying, validating, confirming the patient and creating a publication are write); publishing into the chart still needs the publisher's own direct-care write grant. Approval, about 12:03 UTC: the owner typed "approve 0108" after reading: D-a no 24 h bound; D-b active patient shares count, view-only included -- a view-only share can start, read and check a reading but never publish into the chart, which needs the publisher's own direct-care write; all other 0104 rules kept. Numbered 0108, the next free number after production's 0107. Signed: the owner approved this release in chat on 2026-11-05 (about 12:03 UTC) with "approve 0108"; the coordinator checked that the final scope (D-a and D-b as quoted, every other 0104 D6/D8 rule kept, no other change) matches what the owner approved.
evidence: Single migration 0108_records_processing_cover_lifetime.sql, signed by the owner (see review_reference). WHAT IT DOES: CREATE OR REPLACE of identity.records_processing_direct_care_cover(uuid,text,uuid,uuid,text,timestamptz) (0104 D9) and its comment, nothing else. D-a: the 0104 bound at_time < starts_at + 24 hours is dropped and covered_until (and the ordering key) is the grant's expires_at instead of least(expires_at, starts_at + 24 hours); the cover still ends whenever the grant stops being active (revoked, PIN turned off, held by the cutover, membership or account ended). D-b: one more alternative next to 0104's approval and PIN ways (which are unchanged, now an EXISTS on identity.access_requests by the grant's request_id instead of an inner join): request_id null, no authorization method, granted_by_patient_id = patient_id, and a row in identity.patient_consent_shares with consent_grant_id = the grant, the same patient_id and membership_id; as for every covering grant: purpose direct-care, scope read_records or write_records, not break-glass, active, migration_hold_reason null, source_system 'hid'. Kept exactly from 0104 D6/D8: the same membership at the same facility on the live active account, ocr.job.write at each use, the patient 18 or over on the Africa/Lagos date with a date of birth, deny directives for records processing or direct care (0012's reading), break-glass/emergency and imported or legacy-seeded grants (source_system not 'hid') excluded; 0098's demo share, seeded by a migration with source_system 'hid' in a share's shape, is the one seeded grant that covers, under D-b (the cover's comment and INTERFACE_CONTRACT section 36 say so), both purpose codes active (kill switch). Body md5 f3216bee48827dfba8073199b56ded67 (0104) before, 6928763d3b69f0e4b4acf96a6a255736 after. Signature, result TABLE(consent_grant_id uuid, covered_until timestamptz), owner, language sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, cost, rows, parallel and ACL (hid_identity_runtime EXECUTE only, none for PUBLIC) unchanged, compared attribute by attribute after the replacement. identity.has_active_consent_grant untouched (md5 732d11892dd4e27e1ff9093ae3b7de5a before and after, attributes, owner and ACL compared). No table, column, constraint, policy, trigger, role, permission or grant change; runtime-grants.sql unchanged (its 0104 block names the same signature and applies cleanly twice); no row read or written. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api reads consent_grant_id and covered_until from the cover and answers expiresAt = covered_until (postgres-identity.provider.ts, unchanged but for a comment), so it reports the longer cover with no code change; OCR, EHR documents and every policy reach the cover through has_active_consent_grant by name. PATIENT DISCLOSURE NOT YET IN PLACE: the website's patient wording (0104 decision 34(1), "said clearly to the patient") still says "for up to 24 hours" on the approval, PIN and inbox screens and says nothing about records processing on the share screens; it is the website lane's to update (INTERFACE_CONTRACT section 36, "What the patient must be told (0108)"): D-a drops the 24-hour words; with D-b the share search and confirmation, invitation creation and invitation confirmation screens must say that a share at any level, view_only included, also lets the clinician bring in the patient's paper records (OCR jobs) for the share's duration, up to 365 days. Status at signing: the live approval, PIN and inbox wording already says "while their access lasts" (paperRecordsWording.ts on health main), so D-a needs no website change; the share screens line for D-b (every share level, view_only reading only) is health#168, held so that it ships with this release and not before. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads only; 55000 or 42501, nothing applied): 0001-0107 applied (ocr.claim_worker_job_fair md5 49b95651106e0aaa6f8bf6c8adcdb696 is the marker); not applied yet (the cover's body is not already 0108's, else '0108: already applied'); md5 of the cover (0104's), has_active_consent_grant (0104's), auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff93fe729fd5c5b986b80c9dd6 and identity.write_patient_share e7bce33a905c66e224f0fb7dff513701 (0095's, the share writer); the cover's attributes, arguments and result; the 55 columns read with their types and NOT NULLs (patient_consent_shares consent_grant_id, patient_id, membership_id uuid NOT NULL among them); one owner for identity.access_requests, identity.consent_grants, identity.patients, the cover and has_active_consent_grant, the applier it or a member with INHERIT and SET; that owner holds USAGE/CREATE on identity, USAGE on auth, SELECT on auth.accounts, the directive tables, the memberships, the purpose codes and identity.patient_consent_shares and EXECUTE on auth.membership_has_permission, never through a superuser's bypass; no forced row-level security on the tables the cover reads as its owner, and identity.patient_consent_shares (forced, 0095) has a permissive all-roles policy admitting the owner; the cover's ACL is 0104's. LOCKS (pg_locks before commit on a 0107 copy): ACCESS SHARE on identity.consent_grants, auth.accounts, identity.patients, identity.access_requests, identity.patient_consent_shares, identity.purpose_of_use_codes, identity.consent_directives, identity.consent_directive_versions and identity.staff_facility_memberships; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on the cover (its comment); catalog and the session's temporary objects; nothing on has_active_consent_grant. Apply time about 18 ms. Behind ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on identity.patient_consent_shares the runner stopped after its 5 s lock_timeout with nothing applied; behind a writer of identity.consent_grants it applied at once. PROVED on throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 clusters (created and deleted): FRESH install of all 109 files 0001-0108 with the migrations before the role bootstrap (0 runtime roles before; plan 109 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, 0 pending), role bootstrap and --verify-only pass, the file again answers '0108: already applied', runtime-grants.sql applied twice and the bootstrap run again pass, all 81 database suites pass (records-processing 283 cases). UPGRADE: a database built by base 605e971e's own runner, files and runtime-grants.sql (108 files, ledger last 0107, cover md5 f3216bee...; the updated suite fails there, 50 cases), plan 1 pending (0108 with this sha256), dry run rolled back (cover still 0104's), apply, 0 pending, the runner again applies nothing, the file again answers '0108: already applied'; cover owner, attributes and ACL identical before and after, and identical to the fresh install; 1221 non-owner grants before 0108, after it and after a bootstrap (as on the fresh install); runtime-grants.sql applied twice; all 81 suites pass. services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator (MIGRATION_TARGET=rds, baseline 108 files with the base's runtime-grants.sql, 109 integrated, declared exactly 0108; dry run rolled back, checksums kept, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2480), 188 row-security settings unchanged). Negative copies stop with nothing applied: a 0106 database ('0108: 0001-0107 must be applied first'), a share policy hiding rows from the owner (42501), a changed has_active_consent_grant body (md5 mismatch). MUTANTS: 269 single-condition mutants of the cover body, enumerated from its text (every WHERE and ON conjunct, every alternative of an OR, and every sub-condition of the approval, PIN, share, age and deny-directive tests made true, false or negated; the grant's, directive's and disabled_until's time comparisons and the age comparison made strict or loose; 17 or 19 years, UTC or the session's time zone instead of Africa/Lagos, and dob + 18 years for the age; the action and scope literals and the purpose count; covered_until, the order and the limit), each applied as a CREATE OR REPLACE on a fresh copy of a 0001-0108 database, then the records-processing suite run with its body-md5 case 1g2 set aside (order-routes-cannot-complete's d18 is the other md5 pin and was not run). 255 fail behavioural cases; each directive, age, account, permission, purpose-code and grant condition that applies to both ways is caught on the share (10sk01-10sk55) and on the approval grant (10zk01-10zk55), the request and PIN conditions by 10r3, 10za2-10za8 and 10zk39, the share conditions by 10s21b and 10s26-10s31. 14 are equivalent (no row the tables allow tells them apart from the body, so no case can catch them): dropping at_time is not null (a null at_time already fails starts_at <= at_time) and dropping dob is not null (a null dob fails the age comparison); dropping the account subject test, the account status test or the account join (auth.membership_has_permission checks the request membership's account subject and status at each use, and the exact-membership foreign key makes the grant's account its membership's), the grant facility test and the directive membership's facility test (the same key gives the grant its membership's facility, which the permission check requires to be the request's); dropping the grant scope test alone or the grant break_glass test alone (consent_grants' CHECK makes scope break_glass exactly when break_glass is set for source_system 'hid': 10s46); dropping the request's patient, membership, facility or purpose test (the exact-request foreign key makes them the grant's: 10za10, 10za11); coalesce(permission, true) instead of false (the permission check never answers null). SUITE: services/ehr-api/test/database/records-processing.integration.sql, 283 cases: 1g2 the new body's md5; 5b/6d a share now covers records processing; 10l-10o2 a three-day grant covered 24 hours and two days after its start, until a second before its end, not at its end, covered_until = expires_at; 10p-10q revoked not covered; 10s1-10s24 shares: named by the cover until its expires_at, replaced share no longer covers, view_only covers records-processing read and write while direct care reads only, a 7-day share covered two days on, a seeded (source_system not 'hid') share not covered, another membership or facility not covered, a deny directive for records processing at the share's facility, its withdrawal, revocation, under-18 and no date of birth not covered, a share row on break-glass not covered, a grant with no request and no share row not covered, the kill switch; 10s25-10s46, 10sk01-10sk55, 10r2-10r3, 10za1-10za11 and 10zk01-10zk55: conditions of the cover changed one at a time as the owner in a rolled-back subtransaction and the cover asked directly (see MUTANTS); order-routes-cannot-complete's d18 pin of the cover renewed to 0108's md5.
